Severe bleeding: check scene safety, use clean cloth or dressing and firm direct pressure. Add more cloth without removing soaked layers. If an arm or leg bleed is life-threatening and trained help is available, follow the tourniquet instructions in your kit. Keep the person warm and seek emergency help immediately. Do not use a stick as a tourniquet unless a trained protocol specifically directs it.

Keep the injured area still. Do not straighten it or push exposed bone back. Support it with padding and a splint only if needed for safe movement, using two nearby rigid supports without tightening over the injury. Check circulation before and after. Get urgent medical help.
Lay the person flat if safe, keep them warm, reassure them, and do not give food, drink, or medication if they are confused, vomiting, or may need surgery. Monitor breathing and seek emergency help.

Use the safest source available. Filter visible sediment and boil when possible; chemical treatment must follow its product label. Avoid unknown water if safer water exists. Small frequent sips are safer than forcing a large amount.

Cool a thermal burn with clean running water for about 20 minutes when available. Remove jewelry or loose clothing, not anything stuck to skin. Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy dressing. Do not apply ice, butter, toothpaste, or break blisters.

Check scene safety and responsiveness. Call emergency services or send someone. Check breathing briefly. If the person is not breathing normally, begin CPR if trained and follow dispatcher instructions; use an AED if available.

Keep calm. Check scene safety, identify immediate threats, check responsiveness and breathing, call or signal for emergency help, share your location, and provide only care you are trained to give. This offline guide can be wrong and cannot diagnose or prescribe medication.
